# Ridu 0.23.0

Ridu gzips its JSON and HTML responses, can see each visitor's address behind proxies it can't
list, such as Railway's, and adds `Fit: "inside"` for image sizes that show a whole photo. WebP
uploads now work.

## Fixes

- WebP uploads were refused. Ridu recognised WebP files but had no decoder for them, so a
  collection that allowed `image/webp` failed every WebP upload with "decode image metadata: image:
  unknown format". Ridu now decodes WebP and keeps the original as uploaded. Go can't write WebP, so
  image sizes made from a lossy WebP without transparency are JPEG, and those made from a lossless
  or transparent WebP are PNG. `"contain"` sizes stay PNG for their transparent padding.
- A trusted proxy's `Forwarded` header without a `proto` parameter made Ridu treat the request as
  plain HTTP, ignoring `X-Forwarded-Proto`. Some proxies, reportedly including Railway's, pass a
  visitor's own `Forwarded` header on, so a visitor who sent one couldn't sign in once those proxies
  were trusted. Ridu now falls back to `X-Forwarded-Proto`.
- The Go comment on `UploadConfig.Private` suggested files without it were public. Every download is
  already checked against the collection's read access and sent as `private, no-store`; `Private`
  also requires a signed-in caller. The comment and the uploads guide now say so. See
  [Uploads](https://riducms.com/docs/uploads/).

## Changes

- Ridu gzips `GET` responses of 1 KiB or more that are JSON, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG or other
  text, for clients that accept gzip, and sends `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. Compressed responses get a
  weak `ETag` and no `Content-Length` or `Accept-Ranges`. Responses under `/api/auth/` and responses
  to other methods stay uncompressed, because they can carry session or preview tokens, which
  compression could reveal through the response's length (BREACH). Custom and plugin endpoints
  follow the same rules, so return secrets from `POST` endpoints. On a Railway deployment,
  `/api/schema` went from 60 KB to about 9 KB. See
  [Production](https://riducms.com/docs/production/).
- `HandlerOptions.TrustedProxyHops`, read from `RIDU_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` in generated projects,
  counts the proxies a request passes through when only the one that connects to Ridu can be listed
  in `TrustedProxyCIDRs`. Ridu then takes the client address from before them in
  `X-Forwarded-For`, so sign-in rate limits apply to each visitor instead of the whole proxy. The
  [Railway guide](https://riducms.com/docs/production/railway/#variables) now sets
  `RIDU_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS=100.64.0.0/10` and `RIDU_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=2`. Account lockout
  (`MaxLoginAttempts`) still limits guesses at one account from any number of addresses.
- `Fit: "inside"` fits an image size within its `Width` × `Height` at the picture's own shape,
  without padding, and never enlarges it. The size's stored `width` and `height` are the picture's,
  so they can be smaller than the box. `"contain"` still pads to the full box, as sharp and Payload
  do, and its padding is now documented. See [Uploads](https://riducms.com/docs/uploads/).
- `RequestObservation.ResponseBytes` documents that it counts the bytes the handler wrote, before
  compression.

## Upgrade

Update the Go module and all Ridu npm packages to 0.23.0 together, and rebuild the admin and
application binary.

`cmd/server/main.go` belongs to your project, so the new setting isn't added for you. To use it,
add `TrustedProxyHops: envInt("RIDU_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS"),` after `TrustedProxyCIDRs` in
`HandlerOptions`, and copy the `envInt` helper from a project made with `ridu new`. On Railway, set
the two variables from the Railway guide.

Changing an image size's `Fit` affects new uploads; files uploaded earlier keep the sizes they were
made with.

Ridu requires Go 1.26.9 or newer. Go 1.27.0 and 1.27.1 meet that minimum but still have the
standard-library vulnerabilities described in the 0.20.0 notes, so build and deploy with Go 1.26.9
or a later 1.26 release, or with Go 1.27.2 or later.
